content.title: About
content.content: The “Breakfast Biscuit” crackers are light, dry biscuits designed for a quick morning meal. They are made from wheat flour, vegetable oils, and a modest amount of sugar, giving them a mild taste and crisp texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial batch was launched in 1998.
The formula often includes vitamin B1 (thiamine) to support energy metabolism.
Crackers are packaged in individual serving packets, making them popular for travel.
They are commonly enjoyed with milk, yogurt, or fruit puree.

items.title: Quick source of energy
items.content: Carbohydrates in the crackers are rapidly absorbed, providing an immediate energy boost in the morning.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: B1 and B2 vitamins help support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: Compared with many breakfast options, these crackers have a moderate fat level.

items.title: Convenient and portable
items.content: Lightweight and ready‑to‑eat, they suit busy lifestyles.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Crackers contain wheat flour and are not suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Some varieties may contain added sugar, which should be considered by individuals with diabetes.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: They can raise blood sugar quickly, so pairing with protein or fiber is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Crackers can be eaten plain, dipped in milk, added to yogurt, or used as a base for spreads such as cottage cheese, avocado, or low‑fat cheese.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in a tightly sealed package. For extended storage, keep in the refrigerator to prevent spoilage.
